correctness.rationale: For every nondegenerate fixed triangle in R^3, the projective inner product is exactly cos(theta)-(n.u)(n.v). An orthonormal-bisector change of coordinates makes its negative-sign event an explicit spheroidal quadratic inequality. Two exact spherical integrations reconstruct the same p(theta); the positive integrand proves strict convexity on acute angles. Disjoint obtuse vertices and Jensen yield the unique equilateral minimizer. The polynomial certificate 0<=w<=1 yields p(pi/3)<1/6, removing right/obtuse-source competitors. An arbitrary shape has a positive-measure acute viewing neighborhood by singular-value realization, while a degenerate-shape limit reaches probability one. The existing path verify_projection.py ran and passed 2022 direct checks and 125000 Monte Carlo trials; finite tests are diagnostic only.

originality.rationale: For a fixed Euclidean triangle and a Haar-random orthographic viewing plane, the exact probability of an obtuse projected triangle is the sum of a universal per-angle elliptic integral and has a sharp global lower bound, attained only at equilateral triangles. The full primary arXiv text checked concerns face-count changes for projections of full-dimensional simplices and implies only the trivial constant three-vertex fact for a planar triangle; it does not supply projected Euclidean angle probabilities or a shape-extremal inequality. Published database hits use one-dimensional widths, 3D polytope shadow types, or independently random vertices. Exact statement-level searches gave no known stronger result covering this claim. This is a best-knowledge original assessment, not exhaustive historical priority.

value.rationale: Haar-orthographic viewing of a fixed triangle is a natural basic geometric-probability model. A sharp universal bound over all triangle shapes, an exact continuous-angle formula and unique equality characterization identify unavoidable view-dependent obtuseness and its extremal geometry. The result is not an arbitrary parameter slice, a numerical-table recomputation or a slight adjustment of a known estimate; strict convexity provides a structural extremal mechanism.
